cases.note: Narrowed to the backends that may declare `read: fresh` (the S3 family, OneDrive and SharePoint, the Hugging Face buckets, flat and key-prefixed, the Hub repos, whose hf-hub target changes the file by commit, GitHub, whose target changes it by a contents PUT, Google Drive, whose token is the file's md5, and Dropbox, flat and under a root_path, whose token is the content_hash a listing row, get_metadata and every download's Dropbox-API-Result carry, and Box, whose token is the sha1 a listing row and GET /files/{id} carry; a read checks its bytes against it): ssh, the other, caches reads but stamps no comparable content token, so the mount-time verdict refuses the policy and the workspace never constructs. The bounded control keeps the full list, hf-prefix included so the pair measures the same buckets. The github fake is one shared world, and needs no reset: every scenario starts by writing v1, create or update.

scenario.command: echo aaaa | tee /data/prov.txt > /dev/null; echo bbbb | sed -n 'w /data/prov.txt'

cases.note: tee reports the bytes it wrote; sed's `w` writes the same path later on the line without reporting them, so the newest write record is not tee's and the line keeps nothing: the bounded cat reads what the backend holds, not tee's bytes. Both writes are four bytes, so only the provenance check, not the size check, can drop tee's copy.
